title: Characteristic polynomial and root formula for a polynomial norm
statement:
Let $E$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital $\mathbf Q$-algebra [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], let $d>0$, and let $\delta:E\to\mathbf Q$ satisfy $\delta(1)=1$ and $\delta(xy)=\delta(x)\delta(y)$. Assume that in a rational basis of $E$, $\delta$ is represented by a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$, meaning every nonzero monomial has total degree $d$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For $u\in E$, the function $t\mapsto\delta(t1-u)$ is represented by a unique monic polynomial $P_u\in\mathbf Q[X]$ of degree $d$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. If $L/\mathbf Q$ is a field extension splitting $P_u$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_d\in L$ are its roots counted with multiplicity, then for every $F\in\mathbf Q[T]$,
$$\delta(F(u))=\prod_{i=1}^d F(a_i)\quad\text{in }L.$$
If $u$ is annihilated by a monic polynomial in $\mathbf Z[T]$, then every coefficient of $P_u$ belongs to $\mathbf Z\subset\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.22, printed p.51 (root product identity), with normalization and homogeneity as in Proposition 10.13 and Theorem 10.9, printed pp.47–48. The integral-coefficient conclusion is the general polynomial-norm version of Theorem 10.9; details supplied in the report.

proof.text: Fix a rational basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $E$ and a homogeneous representing polynomial $D\in\mathbf Q[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]$. Write $1=\sum b_je_j$ and $u=\sum v_je_j$. Substitution in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives $P(X)=D(Xb_1-v_1,\ldots,Xb_n-v_n)$. Each monomial of $D$ has total degree $d$, so this has degree at most $d$; its coefficient of $X^d$ is $D(b)=\delta(1)=1$. Thus $P$ is monic of degree $d$, and $P(t)=\delta(t1-u)$ on $\mathbf Q$. Any other representing polynomial agrees with $P$ at the infinite set $\mathbf Q$, hence is equal to $P$ by [lem-trf-polynomial-infinite-evaluation-identity]. Call it $P_u$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.22 and proof, printed p.51; normalization and homogeneity as in Proposition 10.13, pp.47–48. Agent expansion of scalar extension, signs and integrality.

proof.text: The last sentence of [lem-sfb-bounded-line-polynomial-interpolation] says that polynomials over an infinite field are determined by their values on every finite coordinate space. Write $e_i e_j=\sum_k c_{ijk}e_k$ with $c_{ijk}\in\mathbf Q$, and put $m_k(Z,W)=\sum_{i,j}c_{ijk}Z_iW_j$. Multiplicativity of $\delta$ says $D(m(Z,W))-D(Z)D(W)$ vanishes on all rational tuples. Polynomial determination makes this the zero polynomial. For any extension field $K/\mathbf Q$, give $K^n$ multiplication $m$, identity $b$, and componentwise addition; the associativity and unit equations hold because the structure constants satisfy those equations in $\mathbf Q$. Evaluate the same polynomial $D$ on $K^n$ to obtain $\delta_K$. The zero polynomial identity proves $\delta_K(xy)=\delta_K(x)\delta_K(y)$ and $\delta_K(b)=1$. Direct monomial evaluation gives $\delta_K(cx)=c^d\delta_K(x)$, so $\delta_K(cb)=c^d$ and $\delta_K(0)=0$ since $d>0$. Its restriction to rational coordinates is $\delta$, and $\delta_K(tb-u)=P_u(t)$ for every $t\in K$. These constructions use only polynomial evaluation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.22 and proof, printed p.51; normalization and homogeneity as in Proposition 10.13, pp.47–48. Agent expansion of scalar extension, signs and integrality.

proof.text: Let $L$ be the given splitting extension. Choose an algebraic closure $K$ of $L$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; the inclusion $L\to K$ is injective. By [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization], every nonzero $F\in\mathbf Q[T]$ factors over $K$ as $c\prod_{j=1}^m(T-b_j)$, with $c\ne0$ and $m=\deg F$. The same factorization lemma for the monic $P_u$ gives its $d$ linear factors, which are the prescribed $a_i$ transported from $L$. Substitution of $u$ in the factorization of $F$ is valid in the coordinate algebra of step 2: scalars are central and all factors are polynomials in the single element $u$, so they commute even when $E$ is not commutative.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.22 and proof, printed p.51; normalization and homogeneity as in Proposition 10.13, pp.47–48. Agent expansion of scalar extension, signs and integrality.

proof.text: For $F\ne0$, multiplicativity and homogeneity from step 2 give $\delta_K(F(u))=c^d\prod_{j=1}^m\delta_K(u-b_j1)=c^d(-1)^{dm}\prod_{j=1}^mP_u(b_j)$. Substitute $P_u(b_j)=\prod_{i=1}^d(b_j-a_i)$ and reverse each of the $dm$ differences. The two signs cancel, leaving $c^d\prod_{i,j}(a_i-b_j)=\prod_{i=1}^d F(a_i)$. The left side is the image of the rational number $\delta(F(u))$. Both sides lie in $L$, so injectivity of $L\to K$ gives the claimed equality in $L$. This includes nonzero constants ($m=0$, empty products). If $F=0$, its evaluation has norm $\delta(0)=0$, and the right side is zero because $d>0$. All products count the given roots with multiplicity.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.22 and proof, printed p.51; normalization and homogeneity as in Proposition 10.13, pp.47–48. Agent expansion of scalar extension, signs and integrality.

proof.text: For integrality choose a monic $H\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $H(u)=0$. Work in an algebraic closure $K$ of $\mathbf Q$ as supplied by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and factor $P_u$ and $H$ there by [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization]. Let $a$ be any root of $P_u$. The polynomial identity $H(T)-H(a)=(T-a)Q_a(T)$ follows termwise from $T^r-a^r=(T-a)\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}T^{r-1-j}a^j$. If $H(a)\ne0$, evaluation at $u$ gives $(u-a1)Q_a(u)=-H(a)1$, hence $(u-a1)(-Q_a(u)/H(a))=1$. Apply $\delta_K$: the left product has norm $\delta_K(u-a1)\delta_K(-Q_a(u)/H(a))=(-1)^dP_u(a)\delta_K(-Q_a(u)/H(a))=0$, whereas $\delta_K(1)=1$. This contradiction proves $H(a)=0$ for every root $a$ of $P_u$. No claim that $P_u$ annihilates $u$ is used.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.22 and proof, printed p.51; normalization and homogeneity as in Proposition 10.13, pp.47–48. Agent expansion of scalar extension, signs and integrality.

proof.text: In the factorizations of step 5, let $r_a$ be the number of occurrences of $a$ among the $d$ roots of $P_u$, and let $s_a$ be its number of occurrences among the roots of $H$. Whenever $r_a>0$, step 5 gives $H(a)=0$; evaluating the linear factorization of $H$ in the field $K$ shows some factor vanishes, so $s_a\geq1$. Thus $r_a\leq d s_a$ for every $a$. The finite product $\prod_a(T-a)^{d s_a-r_a}$, taken over roots occurring in either factorization, multiplied by $P_u$ equals $H^d$. Therefore $P_u\mid H^d$ in $K[T]$, with explicit quotient even for repeated roots. Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-divisibility-field-extension] to $\mathbf Q\to K$, $p=P_u$ and $q=H^d$: the same divisibility holds in $\mathbf Q[T]$. The integer polynomial $H^d$ is monic, since its leading coefficient is $1^d$. Now [lem-weil-monic-divisor-integral] applies to the monic rational divisor $P_u$ of this monic integer polynomial, and gives every coefficient of $P_u$ in $\mathbf Z$.

Step 5: H(a)≠0 would make u−a1 right-invertible, giving 0=δ_K(1)=1; this is correct and needs no Cayley–Hamilton.
